name: Lap of Love
desc:
Call Center Representative (Veterinary Care Coordinator) | $16 | Veterinary / Pet Care Services


Glassdoor rates the Call Center Representative interview as one of the easiest roles at Lap of Love, with an overall interview difficulty score of 2.56 out of 5 and an average hire time of about 10 days

Lap of Love is a national in-home pet euthanasia and hospice company. This call center role is the intake line for families reaching out about a range of pet care situations. Call types include end-of-life care, quality-of-life care, and pets with behavioral issues such as aggression or bite incidents. That last category matters. A family calling about an aggressive or biting pet is not in grief mode. They may be scared, frustrated, or dealing with an active safety situation. You need to be able to handle that kind of call with the same professionalism as a compassionate hospice conversation.
Your job is to answer a high volume of calls, gather pet medical information accurately, schedule appointments, and document everything in real time while staying calm and focused on the caller. Production and quality standards are tracked. Attendance is strict and non-negotiable per the posting.
This is a fully remote position but it is not a flexible or self-paced role. You are on a set schedule, expected to be present every minute of your shift, and held to daily performance metrics.
assessment:
10 questions. all timed: Listening to a timed set of phone calls with people and animals crying in the background, finding mistakes in the addresses or account info shown, if any. Then you're given paragraphs to read and find the errors, if any. 
On one question you have to find a base price for use of service based on the time of customer and day of the week. 
asked "Taken into account the job posting, why do you think you're a good fit?" 
assessed on active listening skills, corrections, grammar

Candidates report a 20 to 30 minute online assessment completed before the interview stage, followed by a virtual group interview via Google Meet. Overall interview process is rated easy. Total time from application to offer averages about 10 days.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: Not stated. High school diploma or GED is the reasonable floor.
Required Experience:
High call volume, customer service, or call center experience
Prior work-from-home experience strongly preferred
Hard-wired Ethernet internet at home before applying
Preferred Experience:
Veterinary, animal services, or healthcare background
Experience with Five9, Zoom, or Google Workspace
Required Skills:
De-escalation across varied call types
Accurate data entry and documentation during live calls
Appointment scheduling and calendar management
Strict schedule adherence
Ability to shift tone and approach based on caller situation
 Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
Someone with call center experience who handles unpredictable call types without getting rattled
Animal lovers comfortable with the full range of pet care situations
People who are steady under pressure and can move from one emotionally different call type to the next without carrying it forward
Someone with a quiet dedicated home workspace and wired internet already in place
People who want consistent hours even if non-traditional, with overtime availability
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone without hard-wired Ethernet at home
People who struggle with conflict-based or behavioral crisis calls
Anyone with attendance or punctuality challenges
People who need a standard daytime weekday schedule
Anyone who cannot complete the full multi-week training program without interruption
 Top 10 Resume Keywords:
High-volume call center
Customer service
De-escalation
Appointment scheduling
Remote work
Data entry
Animal or veterinary services
Google Workspace
Five9 or VoIP platform
Multi-line phone management
notes:
The call scope here includes behavioral and aggression-related calls alongside end-of-life and quality-of-life conversations. 
Make sure participants understand the full range before they apply. Someone drawn to this work purely for the compassionate support angle needs to know they will also field calls about dangerous animal situations in the same shift.
Company is very repetitive about having an ethernet connection option. Company Equipment is provided. 

Attendance language in this posting is repeated and emphatic. Participants with inconsistent attendance history need that conversation before they apply. The multi-week training program must be completed in full without interruption or the offer is pulled.
.
other:
This is one of the more emotionally demanding customer service roles available. The technical work itself is not difficult, but the subject matter can be challenging because many callers are grieving or facing end-of-life decisions for their pets.
Participants with veterinary clinic experience, healthcare scheduling backgrounds, hospice support experience, caregiving roles, or strong customer service experience tend to perform best.
The pay is relatively low at $16/hour compared to other remote customer service opportunities, so the strongest fit is usually someone who is passionate about helping animals and pet owners rather than someone focused primarily on income growth.
Experience Level: Entry to Mid-Level
Call Volume: High
Data Entry: Moderate
Emotional Intensity: Very High
Sales: None
Schedule Flexibility Required: High (24/7 operation)
Career Path: Veterinary Operations, Veterinary Scheduling, Customer Experience, Healthcare Coordination
